drafts.title: Preserve the car’s strong, smooth acceleration and engaging driving feel
drafts.description: Customers continue to experience powerful, immediate acceleration and smooth, satisfying power delivery that makes everyday driving feel sporty and effortless.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In dealer/customer acceleration trials, at least 85% of participants rate the vehicle’s acceleration as 'strong/peppy' and 'smooth' (scores ≥4/5) across typical launch and overtaking maneuvers.
assumptions: Successor uses a drivetrain that delivers equal or better 0–60 feel than today's G60 in customer perception tests.
Customer perception surveys and standardized drive trials will be used as acceptance tests.
uncertainties: Different customer expectations over time may change the subjective baseline for 'sporty' feel.
Perceived acceleration depends on vehicle weight, tuning and software calibration that may interact with other requirements (efficiency, NVH).
drafts.scope_reason: Customer-facing driving experience to be preserved; no component-level specs included.

drafts.title: Keep the ride comfort and composed handling customers praise
drafts.description: Passengers and drivers feel the cabin is smooth, quiet and comfortable for long trips while the car still responds crisply to driver inputs.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Post-delivery owner surveys show ≥85% rate ride comfort as 'good' or 'excellent' (≥4/5) and standardized objective NVH and vertical acceleration tests match or improve on current G60 benchmarks.
assumptions: Ride tuning and suspension architecture for successor will target similar comfort/handling balance.
Objective test methods and owner surveys are available and comparable to current model.
uncertainties: Packaging or mass changes (e.g., battery size) could affect ride tuning and NVH.
Optional suspension variants may create different owner perceptions across trims.
drafts.scope_reason: Maintain a current strength in customer experience.

drafts.title: Deliver smooth, predictable power delivery across all drive modes and let customers save preferred drive profiles
drafts.description: Power delivery responds consistently and predictably without abrupt surges, lags or jerks, and drivers can create and recall personalized drive profiles (steering, throttle, suspension, HVAC/lighting) that persist across restarts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In road-tests and owner feedback: ≥90% of starts and mode switches show no perceptible surge/jerk reported; users can create and recall at least 3 personalized profiles and switching profiles is done within 2 taps with ≥90% successful recall rate.
assumptions: Powertrain and software calibration teams can tune software to eliminate jerky behavior while preserving responsiveness.
Personalization settings can reliably persist in user profile storage across updates and vehicle power cycles.
uncertainties: Some jerky behavior may be caused by hardware limits or legacy calibration that cannot be fully resolved in successor.
Deep personalization increases complexity of QA and may interact with warranty/support processes.
drafts.scope_reason: Direct customer outcomes around drive quality and customization.

drafts.title: Stop brake squeal, reduce dust and remove grabby feel
drafts.description: Braking is quiet, smooth and predictable from day one; owners do not experience early squeal, grinding noises, excessive wheel dust or a grabby pedal feel.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In pre-market durability tests and a 6-month owner trial, ≤5% of vehicles report audible brake squeal/grinding or complaints about grabby braking; wheel-dust measurements show a measurable reduction vs current baseline in a standardized test.
assumptions: Brake material and pad/rotor pairing can be optimized for successor without compromising braking performance or durability.
A representative owner trial and lab dust/noise tests will be run as acceptance gates.
uncertainties: Brake noise and dust depend on regional road salt, driver style, and aftermarket wheels which may affect complaint rates.
Some trade-offs between low-noise and braking bite may be required.
drafts.scope_reason: Customer-facing brake comfort and perceived quality.

drafts.title: Ensure seats provide better height range and comfortable fit for small and large occupants
drafts.description: Drivers of shorter stature can achieve a clear forward view and comfortable posture; seats provide supportive bolstering that adapts to smaller occupants without uncomfortable pressure and include intuitive controls.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ergonomic tests with anthropometric subjects: at least 95% of participants down to 5'0" can obtain an unobstructed sightline to hood markers without extreme forward tilt; ≤10% of owners report seat bolsters press uncomfortably in a 3‑month survey.
assumptions: Seat mechanism range can be extended through cushion geometry and mounting without major packaging penalties.
Customer acceptance will be validated with anthropometric tests and owner surveys.
uncertainties: Extending seat height range may affect roofline packaging or center-of-gravity targets.
Perceived firmness is subjective and varies by occupant preference; multiple comfort grades may be needed.
drafts.scope_reason: Direct occupant comfort outcome; not a component spec.

drafts.title: Hands-free trunk and Comfort Access work reliably and doors unlock in an intuitive, user-customizable way
drafts.description: Touchless trunk opens when customers perform the expected, simple kick gesture; approaching the car unlocks all doors by default while an obvious setting lets owners choose alternative behavior.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Hands-free trunk opens on first valid attempt in ≥95% of realistic user tests; default approach-unlock opens all doors in 95% of cases and the unlock behavior can be changed within two menu taps.
assumptions: Sensor/algorithm improvements and UX changes are feasible for successor to reduce false negatives/positives.
A clear default setting change in the UX will resolve most confusion about which doors unlock.
uncertainties: Hardware sensor placement or interference from accessories may still cause occasional failures.
Security/privacy trade-offs (e.g., unlocking all doors by default) may require configurable safeguards.
drafts.scope_reason: Customer experience for access and trunk; not prescribing sensors.

drafts.title: Make displayed electric range accurate and stable in real driving
drafts.description: Range estimates match real-world experience and do not jump unpredictably, reducing range anxiety on longer trips including in cold weather.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Under mixed driving conditions including a cold-weather test, the displayed remaining range has a median error ≤10% vs measured consumed energy and a displayed change of ≤±5 miles over a continuous 30-minute drive in steady conditions.
assumptions: Improvements to range estimation algorithms, temperature compensation and battery modeling are available for successor.
Acceptance uses a combination of instrumented road tests and owner feedback.
uncertainties: Extreme driving patterns and accessory use (AC/heater) will still create variability in individual cases.
Battery aging over ownership will change absolute range and must be compensated for in software.

drafts.title: Improve charging speed reliability and provide clear charger availability/compatibility guidance
drafts.description: When customers need public charging the vehicle reaches expected charge-session speeds, scheduled charging starts reliably, and the vehicle helps find compatible and available chargers with clear guidance about adapters/ports.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: When connected to a public DC fast charger rated ≥100 kW and advertised as compatible, the vehicle reaches at least 80% of expected session power within the first 10 minutes in 90% of sessions in field tests; scheduled charging starts within 2 minutes of configured time in ≥95% of cases; navigation shows charger availability and compatibility warning for 95% of nearby chargers in urban pilot regions.
assumptions: Vehicle supports standard charging protocols and can precondition the battery where allowed; cooperation with network providers can improve charger metadata.
Field tests and pilot regions will be used to validate charger availability guidance.
uncertainties: Third‑party public charger reliability and network occupancy are outside BMW’s direct control.
Different charger power limits, temperature, and state-of-charge will affect achievable power in each session.

drafts.title: Make infotainment easier to use: fewer taps for common tasks, clear layout and better screen ergonomics
drafts.description: Drivers can change the most common functions (temperature, fan, volume, media source) quickly with minimal distraction; the display layout reduces clutter and resists becoming a distracting fingerprint magnet.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a driving usability test, ≥90% of participants can change climate temperature, fan speed and audio source within ≤2 touches or a single physical action; in a sunlight readability and smudge test, ≥80% of users rate the screen as 'readable/acceptable' after 1 week of normal use.
assumptions: A combination of UI simplification, dedicated physical controls for primary functions, and anti-smudge surface treatments will be applied.
Usability tests will simulate real driving conditions to validate results.
uncertainties: Some users prefer full touchscreen control; balancing simplification and feature richness requires careful UX design.
Physical control placement may conflict with other interior design goals.
drafts.scope_reason: Direct user interaction improvements; not requiring particular hardware.

drafts.title: Make common vehicle information and trip odometer easy to find and read
drafts.description: Drivers can view odometer, trip mileage and fuel/electric range information quickly from the instrument cluster or steering controls without lengthy menu dives.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a quick-glance test, users can access odometer and trip mileage within ≤3 seconds or ≤2 control presses from a steady driving position in 95% of attempts.
assumptions: Instrument cluster configurable pages and physical steering or stalk controls can be assigned to show key metrics on demand.
User education and default settings will prioritize quick access.
uncertainties: Some instrument cluster layouts or regional regulations may change how certain items are displayed.
drafts.scope_reason: UX change to increase discoverability of basic vehicle data.

drafts.title: Improve mobile-device integration and in-car wireless charging so phones reliably connect and charge without fuss
drafts.description: Apple CarPlay works reliably when a phone is connected and the in-cabin wireless charger consistently charges common phone sizes without repeated repositioning.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In compatibility tests across major iPhone models, CarPlay connects and functions correctly in ≥98% of connection attempts; the wireless charging pad charges 95% of tested phones at their expected wireless rate without repositioning in static and normal driving vibration tests, and physically accommodates phones up to 6.8" diagonal.
assumptions: OEM cooperation (e.g., Apple) or use of certified protocols is available to address CarPlay issues.
Wireless charging pad form factor and magnets/retention designs can be optimized for common phone sizes.
uncertainties: Phone OS updates and third-party accessories can affect compatibility post-launch.
Wireless charging performance depends on phone model and manufacturer restrictions.
drafts.scope_reason: Direct customer-facing device integration and charging requirement.

drafts.title: Make HVAC vents and climate controls discoverable and adjustable with minimal distraction
drafts.description: Drivers can find and aim vents and adjust fan/temperature quickly, without needing to hunt through menus or look away from the road.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In driving simulations, ≥90% of participants can find and change vent direction or fan speed with ≤2 physical actions or taps and without more than a 2‑second glance away from the road.
assumptions: A mix of visible vent hardware or a clear primary climate control will be implemented in successor.
Usability tests will reflect on-road distraction metrics.
uncertainties: Some climate features may remain in software for packaging reasons; trade-offs between physical controls and clean interior surfaces may persist.

drafts.title: Improve practical interior storage and make flat‑tire preparedness obvious and accessible
drafts.description: Owners find useful, covered storage in convenient locations and can quickly locate vehicle guidance and emergency tools for a flat tire (spare/repair kit) or order roadside support.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Vehicle provides at least four distinct, easily reachable covered storage locations (center console, glovebox, door bins, rear-seat pocket); in a usability test ≥85% of participants can locate tire preparedness info or repair kit within 60 seconds. If no full-size spare is offered, an emergency repair kit or inflator is included and instructions are visible.
assumptions: Packaging will allow for one additional covered storage area and a compact repair kit or inflator where a spare is not offered.
Owner documentation and a visible in-car location (glovebox or placard) will be standard.
uncertainties: Market/regional variations (some markets require spares) and trim-level choices may affect standardization.

drafts.title: Improve connected features: voice recognition and in-car hotspot reliability
drafts.description: Voice commands work reliably for common tasks and the vehicle hotspot provides stable connections suitable for streaming and navigation data.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Voice recognition success rate for common commands is ≥90% in a simulated cabin with background road noise; hotspot connection uptime in an urban driving test is ≥95% during 45-minute continuous streaming sessions.
assumptions: Server-side speech models and on-board fallback strategies will be improved and regional telecom conditions are adequate in test regions.
Hotspot performance depends on paired SIM/contract and local cellular coverage.
uncertainties: Third-party network congestion and carrier policies may affect hotspot metrics.
Speech models may need ongoing retraining to maintain accuracy across accents and languages.

drafts.title: Address unmet interior and exterior design comments and offer richer ambient lighting customization
drafts.description: The successor refines interior and exterior styling based on owner feedback and provides multi-zone ambient lighting that customers can customize by color and brightness to create distinct scenes.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Post-launch owner design-satisfaction survey shows ≥85% positive ratings for interior and exterior design updates; ambient lighting provides at least 4 independent zones, ≥5 color presets and adjustable brightness levels, and 80% of users report the lighting meets their expectations in a 2‑week trial.
assumptions: Exterior and interior restyling activities can be validated with customer clinics before production.
Lighting hardware capable of zone control is available for successor packaging.
uncertainties: Design taste is subjective and regional; some design choices may satisfy some customers but not others.
Lighting choices may have implications for electrical load and supplier sourcing.
drafts.scope_reason: Directly addresses multiple unmet design and lighting signals.

drafts.title: Trend-enabled cockpit personalization: richer software-defined interior and wellness features
drafts.description: Customers can personalize the cockpit in software with profiles that include display layouts, lighting, climate presets and wellness features (air quality indicators, personalized climate and suggested breaks) to create a premium, adaptive cabin experience.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a customer trial, at least 75% of participants successfully create a personalized cockpit profile that includes display layout, lighting and climate settings that persist across sessions; wellness features (air-quality indicator and suggested break alerts) are available and correctly trigger in ≥90% of lab scenarios.
assumptions: By the successor launch (3–5 years), software-defined cockpit platforms and sensors for air quality/climate personalization will be mature enough to deploy.
Customers will accept wellness features when presented as optional, privacy-respecting services.
uncertainties: Wellness features require validated sensors and privacy-safe biometric handling which may be subject to regional rules.
Integrating multiple personalization services increases software complexity and OTA update needs.
drafts.scope_reason: A forward-looking customer outcome based on industry trend toward software-defined cockpits.

drafts.title: Conditionally automated highway driving available where permitted and useful
drafts.description: On suitable highways and where legally allowed, customers can engage a higher level of automation for extended hands-free driving that reliably manages lane keeping, speed and density changes, reducing fatigue on long trips.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In permitted jurisdictions and controlled trials, the system enables hands-free highway driving within a clearly defined operational domain and executes extended highway segments (≥30 minutes) without transfer-of-control incidents in ≥95% of supervised trials.
assumptions: Regulatory approvals and regional certification for conditional automation will be obtained for launch markets where the feature is offered.
Necessary perception and monitoring technologies and supplier agreements are available and validated by launch.
uncertainties: Regulatory or supplier delays (as seen in other OEM programs) could postpone full rollout or limit geographic availability.
Customer acceptance and needed human‑machine interfaces for safe handback remain areas of active learning.
drafts.scope_reason: Forward-looking feature that depends on market/regulatory conditions; customer-facing description only.
